How the models performed in testing

YOLO11n detection: 81.8% precision, 68.3% recall, and 81.0% mAP@0.5 on 108 held-out images with 518 labeled gourds. MobileNetV3Large maturity: 84.63% accuracy and 77.89% balanced accuracy on 462 held-out crop images.

These are separate tests of the detector and classifier. They do not measure the accuracy of the complete two-stage scan. A scan's confidence scores are estimates for that photo, not measured accuracy.

Why this began

“The idea began with a son watching his father work.”

A student saw his father struggle to judge different gourds consistently in the field. The work depended on experience, close inspection, and long hours—knowledge that was valuable but difficult to scale.

That observation became a research question: could a camera and a carefully trained model provide farmers with a quick, understandable second opinion?

Built from respect for farmers, and curiosity about how technology can serve their everyday work.

Responsible use

Useful guidance starts with honest limits.

01

Research, not agricultural advice

The tool is an experimental aid and has not been certified for commercial decisions.

02

Check the whole plant

Colour alone may not indicate maturity. Variety, firmness, size, season, and local knowledge still matter.

03

Know the data boundary

The model performs best on scenes similar to its training data and may struggle in new farms or lighting.
